text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Vietnam and Japan have discussed their respective national defence policies as a measure to enhance mutual understanding. The talks took place in Hanoi during last week's official visit by the Permanent Vice-minister of Japan's Defence Agency, Naoaki Murata.

-- The United Nations Development Programme, the Ministry of Justice and the central State Bank of Vietnam held a workshop to discuss laws and regulations to meet the requirements of a transitional financial sector in Vietnam.
-- The government plans to help create about 1.3 million jobs this year compared with 1.2 million in 1996, when the urban unemployment rate was 5.8 percent.
-- Two murders and 31 robberies were among the 337 criminal cases reported to the Hanoi Police Department in the last three weeks, during which 233 people were arrested.

-- A United Nations Industrial Development Organisation (UNIDO) project to bring Vietnam's General Statistics Office and the Hanoi Statistical Office's system of industrial data up to international standards has been completed.
-- The People's Committee of Thua Thien-Hue province is calling for investment in an eight-km, eight-lane road linking Highway No. 1 with the Chan May deepwater port construction site.
-- The Thai Amata City group plans to develop an oil-refining industrial park in Dung Quat, Quang Ngai province.
-- Officials from the central State Bank of Vietnam and Vietcombank will be questioned in court on Monday, the fourth day of the Tamexco fraud trial in Ho Chi Minh City.
-- Some 105,000 boatpeople have returned to Vietnam from refugee camps in Asian countries since March 1989. A further 6,000 are expected to return home in 1997 from camps in Hong Kong and Thailand.
-- The Hanoi People's Committee has reminded residents of the capital ahead of the lunar new year festival of the authorities' tight control over firecrackers and fireworks.
-- The government will stop granting licenses for beer and soft drink joint-ventures.
